title: Hybrid scheduling strategy for tensor/pipeline sync and NCCL pipelining
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Large requests (long prefill sequences and high decode concurrency) suffer from poor GPU utilization and tail latency when tensor parallel (TP) and pipeline parallel (PP) stages are naively synchronized. NCCL collectives for KV cache exchange add stalls that block prefill/decoder overlap. We need a scheduler that coordinates tensor/pipeline roles, chooses kernels adaptively by sequence length/attention sparsity, and aggressively overlaps NCCL work with useful compute to reduce end-to-end latency and cost.

Goal: Design and implement a hybrid scheduling strategy that: 1) decouples prefill and decode where safe, 2) inserts asynchronous NCCL pipelining for key exchanges, 3) triggers alternative kernel paths for short vs long context windows (attention tiling/flash attention variants), and 4) exposes runtime knobs for autoscaling/batching policies. The solution should improve throughput for mixed prefill-decode workloads and reduce 95th/99th latency for large-context requests by at least 20% in internal benchmarks.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by runtime and infra leads
Prototype that schedules prefill and decode across TP/PP without global stall on our 8-GPU and 16-GPU topologies
End-to-end benchmark showing >=20% reduction in p95 token latency for 8k+ context workloads and >=15% throughput improvement for mixed workloads
Kernel selection heuristics that switch to low-memory attention kernels for short sequences and to chunked attention for long sequences with no functional regressions
Automatic fallback to conservative synchronization when NCCL pipelining fails (e.g., network flapping) with readable metrics in Console
implementation_plan: Week 1: Spike to measure where NCCL collectives block prefill/decoder overlap on 8-GPU TPxPP setups; capture timeline traces and annotate hot kernels
Week 2: Prototype asynchronous NCCL staging buffers + CUDA streams per pipeline stage; implement non-blocking all-reduce/all-gather wrappers
Week 3: Integrate kernel selector that considers effective sequence length, KV cache hit rate, and attention sparsity flags; add unit tests for kernel-switch correctness
Week 4: Build scheduler loop that allows decoder microbatches to start on downstream PP stages while upstream prefill finishes KV exchange; add heuristics to avoid cache-consistency races
Week 5: Run stress benchmarks for mixed prefill/decode workloads across 8/16 GPU clusters; measure p50/p95/p99 and tail throughput
Week 6: Add runtime feature flags and observability (traces, per-stage NCCL overlap metrics) and ship behind runtime-1.20 feature gate
risks: Data consistency: overlapping NCCL exchanges with compute risks stale KV reads if ordering rules are incorrect
Portability: non-blocking NCCL and stream ordering can behave differently across driver/CUDA/NCCL versions; might need per-hardware shims
Regression risk: kernel switching must preserve numerical determinism for model outputs — some attention kernels use different accumulation orders
Operational complexity: added scheduling heuristics increase debugging surface for failures during Dedicated/Private deployments
test_plan: Microbenchmarks: synthetic prefill-only, decode-only, and mixed traces with variable batch sizes and context lengths to validate scheduler decisions
End-to-end: run Redwood internal eval suites against model zoo (Llama variants, MPT) to detect any quality regressions after kernel switching
Chaos tests: simulate NCCL transient failures and link flaps to verify safe fallback and observability triggers
Scale tests: run 100 concurrent requests with 8k context on 16-GPU cluster to validate throughput gains and SLO compliance
Regression tests: nightly runs comparing token-by-token outputs for a canonical prompt set to ensure no functional divergence
